results.reasoning: Re-judged after the build was brought to the accepted design. On a throwaway machine from the CLI scenario harness (fixture g2-request-proposes-gone), with no network, `walkdown lint --no-checks` in ~/shop exits 1 with exactly two errors: addressed n-0002 and open n-0003, each named by its thread file and id. Each names the version proposed, the path looked for under shop/designs, adds that the walk would show "not found" there, and says to put the draft back or run `walkdown threads set <id> --proposes <path> --blueprint checkout`. Waived n-0004, whose file is gone too, is not named. The errors come in request-id order: with the thread files renamed so n-0003's sorts first, n-0002 is still listed first. Both remedies work. The command copied from the message, with <path> filled in, succeeds in ~/shop, and putting the cart draft back clears n-0003; lint then exits 0. With a second project on the machine also holding a blueprint called checkout, the short name in ~/shop still resolves to this one and the command succeeds. Run from outside the project with `--blueprint 0001-sp-checkout`, lint names the blueprint by its ID instead, and that command succeeds from there. The capture matches the design apart from --no-checks, which a redline explains, and made-up UUIDs. Edges below 10%: two blueprints of one checkout sharing a name fall back to the ID by construction, and a hint copied from one directory and run in another unrelated one is outside what a printed hint can know.
